newsitem.title: MEXICO: Judge clears Mexican drug lord of charges - report.
newsitem.headline: Judge clears Mexican drug lord of charges - report.

text.p: A Mexican judge on Monday dismissed drugs charges against an accused drug lord, although the alleged trafficker will remain in jail for the time being, state-owned news agency Notimex reported.
Judge Isidro Avelar Gutierrez in the northern state of Sonora cleared Hector "The Blonde" Palma of drugs charges for lack of evidence, Notimex said.

It marks the second time this year that a Mexican judge has dropped drugs charges against Palma, believed to be a major figure in the Sinaloa cocaine cartel. In January, a judge in the western state of Jalisco also cleared the alleged capo of drugs charges.
Notimex said Palma will remain in jail to serve a six-year sentence in Jalisco on weapons charges and still faces drugs charges in the states of Sinaloa and Guerrero and in Mexico City.
Judicial officials in Sonora and officials at Mexico City's Attorney General's office were unavailable for comment on the report.

Monday's decision was the second blow to Mexico's embattled justice system in days. Last week, notorious drug lord Rafael Caro Quintero won an initial appeal against his 40-year jail sentence for the 1985 murder of U.S. anti-narcotics agent Enrique Camarena.
Mexico's anti-drugs record has been a sore point between Mexico and the United States in the past months, following February's arrest of Mexico's top anti-drugs official on drugs corruption charges.
Officials on both sides of the border have estimated that more than two-thirds of the cocaine entering the United States does so through Mexico.
